name: Nissan Skyline GT-R (R32)
h1: Nissan Skyline GT-R R32 (BNR32): specs, RB26 engine and what owners say

us.x: Never sold new in the US. Each car becomes legal to import under the 25-year rule once it is 25 years old by its month of build. R32 GT-Rs were built from August 1989 to November 1994, so every one has qualified since late 2019.

fame.x: Australia’s Wheels magazine nicknamed the R32 GT-R “Godzilla” in its July 1989 issue. Autosport says the name stuck because the car smashed everything in its path on Australian tracks.
The R32 was built to win Group A touring car races. In the Japanese Touring Car Championship it won all 29 races it entered from 1990 to 1993, and took the title every year.

Jim Richards and Mark Skaife won the Bathurst 1000 in an R32 GT-R in 1991 and again in 1992. The 1992 win came after a crash in heavy rain stopped the race, and the crowd booed them. New rules then all but banned the car.

In Initial D, Takeshi Nakazato drives an R32 GT-R. Car Throttle calls it one of the most menacing cars in the series, though it is only lightly modified: a NISMO front bumper, Work Meister wheels and a custom exhaust.

gens.tag: 2.6-liter twin-turbo RB26DETT, 280 PS (276 hp), 5-speed, all-wheel drive. Built for Japan; 100 went to Australia.

variants.name: Skyline GT-R

hp.note: 280 PS at 6,800 rpm, Japan’s gentlemen’s agreement figure (JDM)

top.note: evo’s claimed figure; PistonHeads says 155 mph flat out

trans.note: ATTESA E-TS sends power to the front wheels when needed; HICAS steers the rear wheels above 80 km/h

variants.what: The car that brought the GT-R name back after 16 years. 43,937 R32 GT-Rs were built in all. evo quotes 0-62 mph in 5.6 seconds (Nissan’s claim).

variants.name: Skyline GT-R NISMO

hp.note: 280 PS at 6,800 rpm, the same rated figure (JDM)

weight.note: 30 kg less than the standard car

variants.what: The homologation car for Group A racing. Bigger turbos with steel wheels instead of ceramic, extra aero, and no ABS or rear wiper. All were Gun Grey. Racing rules needed 500; 560 were built.

variants.name: Skyline GT-R V-spec

weight.note: 50 kg more than the standard car

variants.what: Added in February 1993 to celebrate the racing wins: Brembo brakes, 17-inch BBS wheels, a retuned ATTESA system and the NISMO’s aluminum hood and front bumper. 1,396 built.

variants.name: Skyline GT-R V-spec II
variants.what: The last R32, from February 1994. The only change from the V-spec was wider 245/45R17 tires. 1,306 built.

RB26DETT.name: Nissan RB26DETT
facts: Inline-6, DOHC 24-valve, iron block, aluminum head, belt-driven cams
280 PS (276 hp) at 6,800 rpm, 353 Nm (260 lb-ft) at 4,400 rpm in the R32
Two turbos in parallel with ceramic turbine wheels; NISMO and N1 engines used steel wheels
Six individual throttle bodies instead of one

issues.x: Wikipedia says early R32 engines had the crank surface that drives the oil pump machined too small, which can make the pump fail at high rpm. PistonHeads calls failing oil pump drives a persistent RB26 problem that ends in terminal engine damage, and says to look for about 2 bar of oil pressure at idle and 4 bar higher up.
issues.fix: Later engines got a wider oil pump drive (Wikipedia says from the Series 3 R32; PistonHeads says from February 1993). Aftermarket collars and spline-drive kits also fix it.

issues.x: The stock turbos run about 0.8 bar. PistonHeads warns that pushing them past about 1.0 bar can make their ceramic wheels fail and wreck the engine, and that neglect or poor upgrades can make the turbos break apart.
PistonHeads says misfires usually come from a failing coil pack or a bad plug, and the coil loom can cause trouble too. Replacements are cheap.
